settings.note: Each resource carries a `content` block array, rendered at detailUrlPattern. Block types: paragraph, heading, list, checklist, links, callout. Adding a resource = one entry here, no HTML.

items.title: Website Launch Checklist
items.description: Everything worth verifying before a site goes live — content, links, forms, metadata, analytics, redirects and backups.

content.text: Work down this the day before launch, not the morning of. Anything that fails here is cheap to fix now and expensive to fix once traffic arrives.

content.title: Content
items: Every page has a unique title and meta description written for a human
No lorem ipsum, no TODO, no placeholder images left anywhere
Contact details, prices and opening hours match reality
Legal pages present: privacy, terms, cookies

content.title: Links and forms
items: Every internal link resolves — run a crawler, do not click by hand
Every form delivers to a real inbox, tested from an outside address
Form validation rejects bad input and says why
Thank-you and error states exist and are readable

content.title: Technical
items: HTTPS on, HTTP redirects to HTTPS, no mixed content warnings
301 redirects mapped from every old URL to its new home
robots.txt allows what you want indexed and blocks what you do not
sitemap.xml lists real URLs and is submitted to Search Console
404 page exists and offers a route back
Favicon and social share image both render

content.title: Before you sleep
items: Analytics installed and recording a test visit
Backups running and one restore actually tested
Someone other than you has loaded the site on a phone

items.title: Technical SEO Checklist
items.description: The structural fundamentals: titles, descriptions, headings, canonicals, sitemaps, robots, structured data and internal linking.

content.text: The development half of SEO. None of this makes content rank on its own — it removes the technical reasons it would not.

content.title: Structure
items: One h1 per page describing that page's subject
Headings nest logically, not by font size
Real landmarks: header, nav, main, article, footer
URLs are readable, lowercase and hyphenated

content.title: Metadata
items: Title roughly 50–60 characters, primary subject first
Description roughly 140–160 characters, written as a reason to click
Canonical URL on every page, including the homepage
Open Graph and Twitter tags so shared links do not look broken

content.title: Structured data
items: Organization or LocalBusiness on the site
Article on posts, Product on products, FAQPage where an FAQ exists
Only mark up what is on the page and true
Validated in the Rich Results Test

content.title: Never fake reviews
content.text: Review or AggregateRating markup for reviews that do not exist is one of the fastest routes to a manual action. Ship without it until you have real ones.

content.title: Crawl and speed
items: sitemap.xml current, robots.txt not blocking anything important
No orphan pages — everything is reachable by a link
Core Web Vitals measured on a mid-range phone, not your laptop

items.title: Website Planning Guide
items.description: How to define goals, audience, sitemap, content and features before a single pixel gets designed.

content.text: Most website projects run late because of content, not design or development. Deciding the following before anyone opens a design tool is the highest-leverage hour in the whole project.
1. One goal, ranked
What does a successful visit look like? An enquiry, a booking, a purchase, a call. If the answer is five things, the site will do all five badly. Rank them and design for the first.
2. The sitemap
Every page, its purpose, and what it links to. This is where you discover that four planned pages are really one, or that services needs a level of depth nobody considered.
3. The content plan

content.title: For every page, name
items: What it must say, in rough form
Who is writing it, and by when
Which images, logos and documents already exist
What has to be created from scratch

content.text: 4. Requirements, separated
Split must-have from nice-to-have before quoting. Anything involving login, payment, or data that must stay accurate belongs in the first list and changes the estimate.

items.title: Website Content Brief Template
items.description: A page-by-page structure for gathering copy, images and calls to action from a client or your own team.

content.text: Copy this structure per page. Fill in the intent before the words — it is much easier to write a page when you know what it has to achieve.

content.title: Per page, capture
items: Page name and URL
One sentence: what this page is for
Primary action, and where it goes
Audience: who is reading and what they already know
Key message, in one line
Proof: what makes it believable — numbers, examples, credentials
Sections in order, with a rough word count each
Images and documents needed, and who supplies them
SEO: target subject, title, meta description

content.title: Word counts are a kindness
content.text: "About 120 words" is a far easier brief to answer than "write the about section". It also stops one page arriving at 900 words and another at 40.

items.title: Performance Optimization Checklist
items.description: Image formats, script loading, font strategy, caching, layout shift and the measurements that tell you it worked.

content.text: Measure first. Every item below is worth doing, but doing them in the wrong order wastes a day on something that was never the bottleneck.

content.title: Images — usually the biggest win
items: Resized to the dimensions actually displayed
Served as WebP or AVIF with a fallback
width and height set so nothing shifts while loading
Below-the-fold images lazy-loaded

content.title: Scripts
items: Nothing render-blocking in the head
Third-party tags audited — delete what nobody reads a report from
Bundles split so a page loads only what it uses

content.title: Fonts
items: Two weights, not six
font-display: swap so text is never invisible
Subset to the characters you use
Preconnect to the font host

content.title: Verify
items: Before and after numbers recorded for each change
Tested on a throttled connection and a real mid-range phone
Cumulative Layout Shift under 0.1

items.title: Accessibility Quick Checklist
items.description: Practical WCAG basics: semantics, contrast, focus states, keyboard paths, labels and reduced motion.

content.text: Not the full WCAG spec — the subset that catches most real problems, in the order they usually appear.

content.title: Structure
items: Semantic elements: button for actions, a for navigation
One h1, headings in order, no levels skipped
Every image has alt text; decorative images have alt=""
Page language set on the html element

content.title: Keyboard
items: Everything reachable with Tab, in a sensible order
Focus is always visible — never outline: none with no replacement
No keyboard traps; Escape closes dialogs
Skip link to main content

content.title: Forms
items: Every field has a real label, not just a placeholder
Errors say what is wrong and how to fix it
Errors wired with aria-describedby and aria-invalid

content.title: Visual
items: Body text at least 4.5:1 contrast; large text 3:1
Colour is never the only signal
Layout survives 200% zoom
prefers-reduced-motion respected

items.title: UI Design Resources
items.description: A curated list of interface references, layout patterns, spacing systems and design inspiration worth bookmarking.

content.text: References worth bookmarking rather than a list of everything that exists. All free to use.

items.label: WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices — the reference implementation
Refactoring UI — practical visual design for developers
Every Layout — layouts as composable primitives
Utopia — fluid type and space scales

items.title: Free Icon Libraries
items.description: Open-licence icon sets that are actually maintained, with notes on style consistency and licensing.

content.text: Open-licence sets that are actually maintained. Pick one and stay in it — mixing sets is the fastest way to make an interface look assembled.

items.label: Lucide — community fork of Feather, MIT
Heroicons — by the Tailwind team, MIT

content.title: Check the licence before you ship
content.text: Free to download is not the same as free to use commercially. MIT, Apache 2.0 and CC0 are safe; anything requiring attribution needs a line in your credits.

items.title: Reliable Free Fonts
items.description: Typefaces that hold up in real interfaces, with pairing suggestions and loading strategy notes.

content.text: Typefaces that hold up in real interfaces at real sizes, rather than looking good in a specimen.

items.label: IBM Plex Sans — large family, open
Fraunces — old-style serif with optical sizing

content.title: Loading rules
items: Two weights is usually enough — a variable font counts as one file
font-display: swap so text is never invisible
Subset to the characters you use
Self-host if you can; it removes a third-party request

items.title: Image Optimization Guide
items.description: Choosing formats, sizing responsibly, serving responsive sources and avoiding the layout shift images usually cause.

content.text: Images are the single most common cause of a slow site. Four decisions cover almost all of it.
Format

content.title: Choose by content
items: Photographs — AVIF, or WebP with a JPEG fallback
Flat graphics, logos, icons — SVG
Screenshots with text — PNG or WebP lossless
Never a full-resolution camera JPEG straight from a phone

content.text: Size
Resize to the largest size actually displayed, then serve narrower copies with srcset and sizes so a phone never downloads a desktop image.
Loading

content.title: Rules that hold up
items: loading="lazy" on everything below the fold — never on the hero
width and height on every img, so space is reserved
fetchpriority="high" on the largest above-the-fold image
decoding="async" so decode never blocks paint

items.title: Developer Toolkit
items.description: The editors, extensions, CLI utilities and browser tools that earn their place in a daily workflow.

content.text: The tools that earn their place in a daily workflow, rather than everything that exists.

items.label: Can I Use — browser support, before you commit
axe DevTools — accessibility issues in context
web.dev — patterns and Core Web Vitals

items.title: Website Maintenance Plan
items.description: A simple monthly and quarterly schedule for updates, backups, monitoring, content review and reporting.

content.text: Websites degrade quietly. A schedule beats good intentions.

content.title: Monthly
items: Apply platform, plugin and dependency updates
Verify a backup by actually restoring it somewhere
Submit a test enquiry through every form
Check uptime and error logs

content.title: Quarterly
items: Review content: prices, staff, services, hours
Re-measure Core Web Vitals
Scan for broken links and 404s in Search Console
Review analytics against the site's actual goal

content.title: Annually
items: Does the structure still match the business?
Renew domain, SSL and hosting — confirm ownership is still yours
Audit third-party scripts and delete the unused
Review legal pages against current practice

content.title: The failure that actually hurts
content.text: Discovering three months late that the contact form stopped delivering. A monthly test costs a minute and catches it.

items.title: Questions to Ask Before Building
items.description: The questions that surface real requirements early — and prevent the expensive discoveries that arrive late.

content.text: These surface real requirements early. Every one of them is cheaper to answer now than to discover in week six.

content.title: Business
items: What does a successful visit look like, specifically?
How do enquiries reach you today, and what happens next?
Who decides sign-off, and who else must approve?
Is there a date this has to be live for, and why that date?

content.title: Content
items: Who is writing the copy?
Do brand assets exist — logo files, fonts, photography?
How often will content change, and who changes it?

content.title: Technical
items: Does anyone need to log in? What can they see or do?
What systems must it connect to — CRM, payments, email, stock?
Where is the domain registered, and who controls it?
Is there an existing site with traffic worth preserving?

items.title: CSS Architecture Guide
items.description: Design tokens, layering, naming and file structure that keep a stylesheet maintainable past month three.

content.text: A stylesheet becomes unmaintainable through a hundred small decisions, not one big one. These conventions prevent most of them.
Tokenise every decision
Colour, spacing, type scale, radius, shadow, motion and z-index all live as custom properties in one file. The discipline is refusing to write a raw value once the tokens exist.
Layer in cascade order

content.title: Load in this order
items: variables — tokens only, no rules
base — reset and element defaults
layout — containers, grids, section rhythm
components — reusable pieces
sections — composition of components
utilities — single-purpose helpers, must win over components
responsive — breakpoint corrections, must win over everything

content.text: Rules worth keeping

content.title: In practice
items: One definition per component — no page-specific variants
A fixed spacing scale; never an arbitrary pixel value
!important only to beat a third party you do not control
If a pattern needs three utilities every time, make it a component
